html:
The Piapoco, who call themselves Tsase, are an Arawakan-speaking people of the eastern plains of Colombia, along the Guaviare, Vichada and Meta rivers, with a few communities in Venezuela. These rivers drain into the Orinoco.

They live by fishing, hunting and farming bitter manioc, and in colonial times they traded along the rivers with Spanish and Dutch traders. Like other peoples of the plains, they suffered from slave raiding, missions and later cattle ranching. Their language belongs to the Arawakan family, which once stretched from the Caribbean to Bolivia.
